scope: Normal Release execution with GGML_VULKAN_DEBUG=OFF. Separate DEBUG receipts establish the recorded dispatch controls.
Timings cover resident SCALE followed by MUL_MAT plus submission and synchronization. Allocation, upload, host reference work, and readback are outside the timed interval.

Each mode/case has one separately recorded first computation and 15 warm samples. Dense mode order alternates by case and is reversed in the second process; MMVQ auto/disable uses ABBA process ordering.
Dense mode arithmetic is qualified by its separate 597-graph native DEFAULT N1 fixture. Performance-mode finite/nonzero/repeat checks are not a cross-mode numerical-equivalence gate.
The mode-20 cost rises for larger N in this fixture. The measurements do not establish full-model throughput or expert-indexed projection latency.
Q4_K at N=8 had auto medians 63.05–63.54 us and disabled medians 77.14–77.38 us. Other cases showed noise or no advantage, so no general MMVQ acceleration claim follows.
No clock or power lock was applied. Full raw samples and IQRs remain available for inspecting variance.

notes: A/B/C runtime bytes did not change between final qualification and these implementation commits.

Two trailing blank lines in the dense fixture were removed after performance/source-isolation execution. The final seam rebuild passed 20/20; the normal performance executable digest remained identical.
Documentation was completed after runtime qualification.

profile.name: native A RERoT with resident F32 K/V and batch-invariant projection request
profile.backend_comparison: CPU and Vulkan each compare with their own controls; their generated trajectories are not required or claimed to equal one another.

support_boundaries: Resident unified F32 K and V only, with flash attention off and the recorded public reader capability restrictions.
F16, mixed, or quantized reader KV remains unqualified/refused. Earlier failed F16 receipts are not promoted.
The tested native CPU and single RADV Vulkan execution profiles do not qualify other architectures, optional CPU compute providers, CUDA/HIP/Metal, or other Vulkan devices.
The precision getter records the requested context configuration; public operator checks and independent DEBUG traces establish their own executed scope.
The tiny F64 oracle covers full rotary NORMAL/NEOX with the specified head layout and amplitudes; it is not a full 8B-model oracle or partial-RoPE qualification.
The present native C route submits one opaque A domain. It is not a whole-model TP5 provider.
One-device layer placement does not establish multi-device PP overlap or Vulkan row split support.
LateBind and MTP providers remain absent and are refused explicitly. Unverified archived implementations were not migrated.
Recurrent rollback/replay profiles are outside the tested n_rs_seq=0 path; the GROVEMOE warmup count boundary has no real-model qualification here.

SIGINT/broken-pipe process checks do not identify the exact GPU instruction at signal delivery or independently establish all-device drain. The native cancellation fixture separately checks actual CPU graph abort, drain, and sticky failure.
These RERoT profile gates do not qualify every stock Vulkan backend-op configuration. The earlier full-suite FlashAttention failure remains a historical failure.
Legacy automatic planning, reasoning/tool routing, heuristic template probes, multi-device providers, and speculative decoding remain separate rewrite candidates.
identity_rule: Use the recorded manifest/source maps, implementation commits, installed artifact digests, model digests, and receipt hashes together. A PASS applies only to its stated workload and artifact identity; later edits require the corresponding requalification.
